title: Configurator wizard for heterogeneous workload batching & cache
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Background:
Redwood Console currently exposes low-level knobs for batching and prefix/KV caching but customers struggle to choose safe, cost-effective settings for mixed workloads. Enterprise users, platform teams, and PLG customers need a guided flow that: identifies workload characteristics, offers tailored presets, simulates cost/latency tradeoffs, and exports enforceable policy JSON for rollouts.

Objective:
Design a step-by-step configurator wizard that recommends batching and cache policies for heterogeneous workloads (chat, completion, embeddings, reranking). The wizard should: detect route patterns, let users define workload segments, surface conservative and aggressive suggestions, show percentile latency/cost previews, and include explicit guardrails with rollback suggestions.

User stories:
- As an SRE, I want to apply different batching/caching presets per route so latency-sensitive chat routes remain under SLOs while background embedding routes save cost.
- As a Product Engineer, I want a simulator that shows the expected 95th latency and token cost impact before applying a policy.
- As a Platform Owner, I want exportable policy JSON and a canary rollout plan that hooks into existing rollout controls.

Proposed flow (high level):
1) Onboarding screen: auto-scan routes (or allow manual import) and show workload heatmap by QPS, token distribution, request type.
2) Segment & Suggest: group routes into workload segments (suggested by heuristic), show a recommended preset for each (e.g., \"Ultra-low-latency\", \"Balanced\", \"Cost-first\") with rationale.
3) Scenario simulator: sliders (QPS, prefix-hit-rate, burstiness) + workload sample -> show simulated P50/P95 latency, token-per-request, and monthly cost delta. Visualize a confidence band.
4) Guardrails & risk calibration: show potential failure modes (cache cold-start, increased CPU tail) and recommended limits (max batch size, max wait time, fallback model). Allow enabling automatic fallback to a cheaper variant during overload.
5) Review & export: side-by-side diff of current vs proposed policies, one-click export to policy JSON, optional create rollout with canary parameters and alerting hooks.
6) Rollout monitor link: after applying, surface a short link to the rollout dashboard with cost/latency comparisons.

Design deliverables:
- High-fidelity Figma prototype for the full wizard (desktop) with all states (empty routes, single segment, multiple segments, errors)
- Interactive mini-prototype for the scenario simulator (controls + chart overlays)
- Microcopy copybook for explainers and guardrail rationales
- Acceptance criteria and handoff tokens for engineering (components, props, telemetry events)

Key design constraints and notes:
- Must be usable by non-expert engineers; keep language plain and provide tooltips for technical terms (KV hit, batching window).
- Simulator is probabilistic; clearly annotate uncertainty and recommended conservatism for production rollouts.
- Exported policies must be idempotent and compatible with existing runtime config schema (coordinate with ENG runtime team).
- Accessibility: keyboard-navigable wizards, high-contrast charts, and aria labels for interactive controls.

Metrics for success:
- Time to produce a safe policy for a new route (target: <30 minutes for novice user)
- Reduction in manual tuning cycles reported by SEs by 40% in the first quarter after launch
- 0 major incidents attributable to default suggestions in first 3 months

Acceptance criteria (summary):
- Wizard prototype demonstrates full flow from route discovery through export and creates a JSON policy that matches runtime schema in at least two example cases.
- Simulator displays P50/P95 and cost delta with a confidence band and respects user-adjusted sliders.
- Guardrails screen enumerates at least three automated mitigations and allows enabling/disabling them per segment.
- Handoff includes component library tokens and a telemetry spec with event names and payload examples.

Notes for ENG collaboration:
- Sync with ENG-8421 (batching-runtime-heuristics) to confirm parameter names and allowable ranges.
- Pair with Runtime team on a small validation dataset to power the simulator accuracy (synthetic traces + anonymized telemetry).

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Users blindly accept aggressive presets -> Mitigation: require explicit two-step confirmation for \"Aggressive/Cost-first\" presets and surface historical examples.
- Risk: Simulator mismatch with production -> Mitigation: attach a confidence label and offer a calibration run that replays a short trace in staging.

Next steps:
- Usability test with 6 participants (mix of SE, SRE, PM) scheduled 2026-03-08 to 2026-03-12.
- Iterate prototype based on test results and handoff to ENG for spike (estimate: 2 sprints).
acceptance_criteria: Prototype demonstrates route discovery, suggestion, simulation, guardrails, and export
Simulator shows P50/P95 and cost delta with confidence bands
Exported policy JSON validates against runtime schema for two sample routes
Guardrails page provides at least three automated mitigations with toggles
